cards.prompt: In Portfolio Build 1 (Dual-Bank UART Bootloader), why must the bootloader verify a CRC-16/SHA-256 over the inactive bank BEFORE updating the boot-active metadata flag?
cards.answer: To ensure a power loss or corrupted UART transfer mid-flash never bricks the MCU, allowing automatic fallback to the known-good bank.
accepted_answers: prevent bricking on power loss or corrupted update
cards.explanation: Writing the 'valid' flag last makes firmware updates power-fail atomic.

cards.prompt: In Portfolio Build 2 (RTOS-to-Linux Edge Gateway), why do we bridge a real-time RTOS microcontroller to an Embedded Linux SBC instead of running motor control directly in standard Linux user space?
cards.answer: The RTOS guarantees deterministic microsecond-level hard real-time ISR/control loops, while Linux handles high-level networking, storage, and UI.
accepted_answers: rtos provides deterministic hard real-time while linux handles networking
cards.explanation: Asymmetric multiprocessing (MCU + MPU) pairs hard real-time determinism with rich POSIX networking.

cards.prompt: Which Linux command-line benchmark proves that your `PREEMPT_RT` kernel build meets bounded worst-case scheduling latency under stress?
cards.explanation: `cyclictest` measures the delta between scheduled timer wakeups and actual thread execution in microseconds.

cards.prompt: How does Embedded Rust's Type-State pattern prevent a programmer from reading an uninitialized SPI or UART peripheral at compile time?
cards.answer: By encoding peripheral states (`Disabled`, `Enabled`) as zero-sized generic type parameters so `.read()` only exists on `Peripheral<Enabled>`.
accepted_answers: encodes hardware state in generic types so invalid methods do not exist
cards.explanation: Zero-sized type parameters enforce hardware state machines at compile time with zero runtime RAM or CPU overhead.

cards.prompt: In Portfolio Build 3 (Edge Vision Tracking Turret with a <35 ms glass-to-glass budget), list the four sequential stages that consume that latency budget.
cards.answer: 1) Camera exposure & frame capture, 2) Preprocessing & ONNX/TensorRT inference, 3) PID/EKF control computation, 4) CAN/PWM actuator command response.
accepted_answers: capture, inference, control math, actuator command
cards.explanation: Measuring timestamps at every stage boundary lets you prove mathematically where every millisecond goes.

cards.prompt: In Portfolio Build 4 (Hardened Smart-Factory Cell), how do ECDSA Secure Boot, ATECC608A, and mTLS OPC UA work together as defense-in-depth?
cards.answer: Secure Boot verifies local firmware authenticity at power-on, ATECC608A protects private keys in tamper-resistant hardware, and mTLS authenticates both client and server over the network.
accepted_answers: secure boot verifies firmware, atecc608a protects keys, mtls authenticates network peers
cards.explanation: Combining hardware root-of-trust, key isolation, and mutual TLS protects the device at rest, at boot, and in transit.

cards.prompt: What are the five empirical engineering artifacts you should include in every LLC / capstone GitHub repository to stand out to aerospace/robotics recruiters?
cards.answer: 1) KiCad schematics/wiring diagrams, 2) CMake + GitHub Actions CI, 3) Zero-warning static analysis (clang-tidy/cppcheck), 4) Doxygen docs, 5) Logic analyzer/timing/cyclictest proofs.
accepted_answers: kicad schematics, cmake ci, static analysis, doxygen, timing proofs
cards.explanation: Showing oscilloscope/logic-analyzer screenshots and CI badges proves your firmware works on real hardware, not just in theory.

cards.prompt: Give an example of a valid Conventional Commit message for adding an I2C driver for the BME280 sensor.
cards.answer: feat(i2c): add bare-metal BME280 temperature and pressure driver
cards.explanation: Conventional Commits (`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`) keep your commit history clean and recruiter-readable.

cards.prompt: Why should hard real-time embedded firmware avoid dynamic heap allocation (`malloc` / `new`) after system initialization?
cards.answer: To eliminate non-deterministic allocation latency, heap fragmentation over long uptimes, and out-of-memory crashes.
accepted_answers: eliminate heap fragmentation and non-deterministic latency
cards.explanation: Pre-allocating static pools and ring buffers at startup guarantees deterministic O(1) memory behavior for years of continuous uptime.
